title: How David Goggins builds a callused mind: belief over hope, the Goggins alter ego, and feelingless discipline
summary: Goggins explains the philosophy behind Never Finished: discipline learned from Sergeant Jack, belief earned through work rather than hope, and the Goggins alter ego he summons when suffering peaks. He also covers taking souls, turning hate into fuel, choosing foxhole partners, and shutting off feelings to grind.

principles.text: Hope is not in your hands; belief earned through hard work is.
principles.quote: It's the belief that you harness through hard work and dedication. And it's something that you know what you are capable of because you've gone there several times in those dark times.

principles.text: Take pride in finishing small tasks fully; it builds internal self-respect without needing praise.
principles.quote: I don't need someone to say, 'Good job, David.' I don't need a [ __ ] pat on the back. Everything became internal.

principles.text: Build a visualized alter ego and call on it when suffering peaks; the pain stays, only your mindset changes.
principles.quote: The only thing that changed was how I approached the situation. I no longer wanted to be a victim of that race, a victim in my mind.

principles.text: The real enemy is yourself; nobody will save you, so stop looking for an escape goat.
principles.quote: I realized that I was the true devil. I was the one holding me back. I was the one looking for the escapegoat.

principles.text: Turn haters into fuel by studying the mind of the weak and looping their criticism.
principles.quote: You'll never meet a hater doing better than you, my friend. And that is the truth.

principles.text: To achieve greatness, switch your feelings off when the alarm rings and the grind calls.
principles.quote: Turn your feelings off when it comes down to you wanting to be better. What that means is when that alarm clock goes off, your feelings got to go away.
